title: Company-wide policies and processes (Access, Change, Data, Procurement, Vendors, Travel, Templates)
author: Maya Patel
body:
Overview
========
This document consolidates Redwood Inference's company-wide policies and standard operating procedures for: access & permissions, change management, data management, procurement & expenses, vendor management, travel, and internal templates. It is intended as the canonical reference for employees, managers, and partners.

Scope
-----
Applies to all Redwood employees (full-time, part-time, contractors), vendors with access to internal systems, and any third-party integrators working under a contract that grants access to Redwood resources.

Purpose
-------
- Provide consistent, auditable processes for security, compliance, and operational efficiency.
- Define ownership and escalation paths.
- Set thresholds and SLAs for common workflows (access requests, change approvals, procurement).

Ownership & Contacts
-------------------
- Document owner: People Ops (owner_team).
- Security owner (policy review and enforcement): Security & Compliance (Priya Nambiar).
- Finance owner (procurement & expenses): Finance (Carlos Mendez).
- Change management contact: Eng Platform (Jordan Lee).
- Questions / Exceptions: policies@redwood.ai

1) Access & Permissions
------------------------
Intro
-----
Access to Redwood systems follows the principle of least privilege (PoLP). Access is role-based where possible (RBAC) and time-limited for ad-hoc requests. All access requests and entitlement changes must be recorded in the Access Request system (internal ticketing link).

Roles & Responsibilities
- Requester: employee or manager who needs access; must provide business justification and expected duration.
- Approver: designated owner of the target resource (service owner, data owner).
- Access reviewer: quarterly reviewers for high-privilege roles (Security schedules and maintains reviewer rosters).

Access Request SLA
- Normal requests: processed within 3 business days.
- Elevated / privileged access: processed within 5 business days and require approval from Security.
- Emergency access: temporary access can be granted by an on-call approver and must be logged and followed up with a formal request within 24 hours.

Provisioning Standards (table)
- Resource type | Default role | Approval required | Review cadence
- CI/CD (build, deploy) | developer | Team lead | Quarterly
- Production cluster | read-only / operator | Service owner + SRE lead | Monthly for operators
- Billing & finance consoles | finance | Finance manager | Quarterly
- Customer data stores | data-reader / data-writer | Data owner + Security | Monthly

Deprovisioning
- Managers must submit termination/deprovision tickets within 1 business day of employment end or role change.
- Automated offboarding runs every 24 hours to detect accounts not marked as active.

Access Reviews & Attestation
- High-privilege roles: monthly attestation.
- All roles: minimum quarterly attestation by resource owners.
- Non-attested access for >60 days will be revoked pending re-approval.

2) Change Management
--------------------
Objective
- Maintain system reliability and auditability for production and shared services by standardizing change approvals, scheduling, and post-change verification.

Change Categories
1. Standard changes: low-risk, pre-approved (example: routine certificate rotation, periodic backup jobs).
2. Normal changes: require RFC (Request for Change) and approval; scheduled during maintenance windows.
3. Emergency changes: applied outside normal windows to mitigate active incidents; require post-facto RFC and retrospective.

Process (numbered)
1. Submit an RFC via the Change Management board (include impact, rollback plan, verification steps, and owners).
2. Risk assessment by Change Coordinator (Low/Medium/High).
3. Approval routing: Low -> Team Lead, Medium -> Service Owner + Change Coordinator, High -> SRE Manager + Security + Product.
4. Schedule in maintenance window (default windows: weekdays 23:00-03:00 UTC; weekends 02:00-06:00 UTC).
5. Execute change; run verification checklist.
6. Close RFC with post-change notes and monitoring summary.

Emergency changes
- Emergency changes may be executed with the on-call engineer and incident commander approval. An RFC must be submitted within 24 hours and a postmortem scheduled within 5 business days.

Change Metrics & SLOs
- RFC review turnaround: 2 business days for Normal changes.
- % changes with successful rollbacks tested: target 95%.

3) Data Management
------------------
Principles
- Classify data (Public, Internal, Confidential, Restricted).
- Store and transmit data according to classification and regulatory requirements.
- Minimize data retention and apply encryption at rest and in transit.

Data Classification (table)
- Classification | Description | Handling rules
- Public | Information safe for public release | No encryption required; no PII
- Internal | Company-internal operational info | Access controls; encryption recommended
- Confidential | Customer or proprietary business data | Encryption at rest & transit; logging; RBAC
- Restricted | Highly sensitive PII / regulated data | KMS-backed encryption, strict approval, data residency controls

Retention & Deletion
- Default retention for logs: 90 days (prod logs), 365 days (security logs).
- Customer data retention: per contract; default retention 2 years unless otherwise specified.
- Deletion request procedure: submit Data Deletion ticket with record identifiers and legal approval if required.

Data Handling Requirements
- All confidential and restricted data must be stored in approved systems only (see Approved Systems list).
- Use field-level encryption for high-sensitivity fields.
- Backups containing confidential/restricted data must be encrypted and have a documented retention policy.

Third-party Data Sharing
- Minimum required data only; use Data Processing Agreements (DPAs) for vendors processing customer data. Security review required for any vendor that stores or processes Confidential/Restricted data.

4) Procurement & Expenses
-------------------------
Procurement Principles
- Centralize vendor contracts via Finance. Obtain at least one quote for purchases <$10k and three quotes for purchases >=$50k unless using a preferred vendor.

Approval Thresholds (table)
- Amount | Approval required
- <$250 | Individual contributor (manager notified)
- $250- $5,000 | Manager approval
- $5,000- $50,000 | Manager + Finance (procurement team)
- >$50,000 | Manager + Finance Director + Legal review

Purchase Process (numbered)
1. Create a Purchase Request in the Procurement system with business justification, vendor details, and budget code.
2. Finance verifies budget and compliance with existing contracts.
3. Obtain required approvals per threshold.
4. Procure via corporate card (for approved < $5,000) or Purchase Order (PO) for larger amounts.
5. Finance records vendor and contract metadata (term, renewal, termination clause).

Expense Reimbursement
- Submit expenses in the Expense system within 60 days of incurring.
- Receipts required for all expenses >$25.
- Travel expenses must follow Travel Policy (see section 6).

Preferred Vendors & Discounts
- Preferred vendors are maintained by Finance and Technology Procurement. Use of preferred vendors is encouraged to obtain volume discounts and standardized contracts.

5) Vendor Management
--------------------
Vendor Risk Levels
- Low: marketing vendors, event services — no access to sensitive systems or data.
- Medium: SaaS providers with internal data access but no customer data.
- High: vendors storing or processing Confidential/Restricted customer data or with administrative access.

Due Diligence Requirements
- Low: basic business validation and contract.
- Medium: security questionnaire + SOC 2 Type II or equivalent if handling internal data.
- High: full security assessment, penetration test evidence or attestation, DPA, and contractual right to audit. Legal and Security must sign off on High-risk vendors.

Contracting & Renewal
- All vendor contracts must be stored in the central Contract Repository with expiration and renewal reminders set 90 days before term end.
- Termination clauses and data return/destruction clauses must be explicitly included for any vendor that processes customer data.

Vendor Onboarding Checklist
1. Business approval and budget assignment.
2. Risk classification and security review.
3. Contract negotiation and signatures.
4. Technical onboarding and least-privilege access provisioning.
5. Add to Vendor Registry with point-of-contact and contract metadata.

6) Travel Policy
----------------
Booking & Class
- Domestic coach flights: economy. Exceptions for flights >6 hours may be booked in premium economy with Manager approval.
- International: premium economy standard for flights >8 hours; business class requires VP approval.
- Hotel: business or business-plus; use preferred partners where available.

Per-diem & Allowable Expenses
- Meals: up to $75/day domestic; up to $120/day international (adjusted by region).
- Ground transport: ride-share or standard taxis; car rental limited to mid-size vehicles unless preapproved.

Pre-approval & Booking
- All travel >$1,000 must be pre-approved by manager and Finance.
- Use corporate travel portal for booking to ensure compliance and preferred pricing.

Expense Reporting & Receipts
- Submit travel expenses within 30 days. Itemize expenses and attach receipts. Expenses without receipts >$25 may be declined except in exceptional circumstances with written explanation.

Safety & Emergency
- Employees traveling on company business are required to register trips in the Travel Registry and provide emergency contact information. Company travel insurance covers business travel per the policy document (link).

7) Internal Templates & Forms
----------------------------
Canonical templates are stored in the Templates Library (internal link). Key templates include:
- Access Request template (fields: requester, role, justification, duration).
- RFC template for Change Management (impact, rollback, verification, approvers).
- Purchase Request template (vendor, quotes, justification, budget code).
- Vendor Risk Assessment questionnaire (security and privacy controls).
- Travel authorization form.

Usage Guidance
- Always start from the canonical template; do not use ad-hoc or personal storage for approvals.
- Keep templates up-to-date: template owners must review annually.

Enforcement, Exceptions & Auditing
--------------------------------
- Exceptions: Requests for exceptions must be captured in an Exceptions Register and include a risk acceptance statement signed by the owning team and Security or Finance as appropriate.
- Non-compliance: repeated non-compliance may trigger disciplinary action per People Ops policy.
- Auditing: Internal audit and Security will perform annual audits of access, procurement, data retention, and vendor compliance. Audit findings will be tracked to closure by the responsible teams.

Revision History
----------------
- 2024-11-10: Initial consolidated version authored by Maya Patel.
- 2025-06-18: Updated procurement thresholds (Finance).
- 2026-03-04: Clarified access SLAs and added travel pre-approval thresholds (published).
